key_insight: Machine-learning-driven simulations show that Al content controls whether (MoCrTi)Al refractory HEAs undergo one or two ordering transitions, with B2-type chemical ordering strongly linked to enhanced stiffness.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests alloy composition can be tuned to maximize high-temperature structural performance by exploiting short-range order rather than relying on random solid-solution strengthening alone.
method: Temperature-dependent thermodynamics, short-range order, and elastic-property analysis
evidence_signal: The abstract reports heat capacities and short-range-order parameters across multiple compositions, revealing single- versus double-transition behavior and corresponding changes in elastic constants and moduli.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on the fidelity and transferability of the trained interatomic potential, so validation against experiment or first-principles data remains important.
paper_title: Study of ordering in (MoCrTi)$_{100-x}$Al$_x$ refractory high-entropy alloys using machine learning interatomic potential
